description:
The release archive carries the assembled workflow package beside the binaries, so an adopter who unpacks one download can apply it offline with no second fetch, and the release's own smoke path proves it.

## Background

The archive is flat and carries four files: the two binaries and the two license texts. The workflow package has never been among them, because it travelled inside the binary. Once it does not, an adopter has to obtain it, and the release is where it comes from.

It arrives in the same archive. A separate asset would mean a second download and a second checksum step before a repository can be initialized, which is what the offline promise exists to avoid; putting the directory beside the binaries keeps one download sufficient, adds no asset to the published set, and leaves the existing checksum covering it. The binaries stay at the extraction root so the documented install step still holds, so the package goes under a directory rather than beside them.

The smoke path is what makes it more than a file in a tarball. It already extracts the archive into a clean prefix and initializes a repository through the profile quickstart, naming the profile with no location — which resolves nothing once the compiled-in copy goes. Pointing it at the extracted package proves the published bytes apply, and it proves it from the moment they are published rather than from the moment the compiled-in copy is removed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The archive carries the assembled workflow package directory beside the binaries and the license texts, with the binaries still at the extraction root.
- [hard] REQ-02: The published asset set is unchanged — no asset is added — and the existing checksum file covers the archive that now carries the package.
- [hard] REQ-03: The archive-verification step asserts the package directory is present in the extracted prefix.
- [hard] REQ-04: The smoke path initializes a repository from the extracted package rather than from the binary or a checkout, and asserts over what the resolver enumerates from that location.
- [hard] REQ-05: Any job the change introduces is declared in the workflow contract, so no undeclared workflow or job enters.

## Notes

This lands before the compiled-in copy is removed, so no published release exists in which the profile is reachable only from a source checkout. The archive gains a second package directory when the vocabulary that one depends on becomes a package of its own.
title: Carry the assembled package in the release archive
